name: CD4033BE
title: CD4026B, CD4033B: CMOS decade counters/dividers with decoded 7-segment display outputs
summary: Two 20 V CMOS decade counters, each a Johnson counter and a 7-segment decoder in one 16-pin package, for driving one digit of a numeric display. CD4026B adds a display-enable input that gates the segments, a display-enable output and an ungated c segment; CD4033B adds ripple blanking of leading and trailing zeros and a lamp test. Both count on the rising clock edge with a Schmitt-trigger clock input, typically to 11 MHz at 10 V, and give a carry output for chaining decades. CD4033BE is the CD4033B in a 16-pin plastic DIP.
key_figures: 3 V to 18 V recommended, 20 V absolute maximum

circuits.title: Driving a common-cathode LED display through emitter followers
circuits.description: Each segment output drives the base of an NPN emitter follower whose collector sits on VDD. The emitter feeds its LED segment anode through a series resistor that sets the segment current; the display cathodes share ground. CLOCK INHIBIT and RESET are tied low so the counter runs from CLOCK. Conditions given: VDD at least 3.5 V, about 5 mA per segment, 100 % duty cycle.

circuits.title: Driving a common-anode LED display through saturated switches
circuits.description: Each segment output drives an NPN common-emitter switch through a base resistor. The collector pulls its LED segment cathode down through a series resistor; the display anodes share VDD. A high segment output turns the transistor on and lights the segment. CLOCK INHIBIT and RESET are tied low.
notes: Segments b to f each have the same switch and resistors; the stages for a and g are given.
VDD ≥ 5 V (min); IB ≥ 0.4 mA; IF ≥ 12 mA per segment at 100 % duty cycle; βdc (min) ≥ 30; VCE(sat) ≤ 0.5 V.

circuits.title: Driving an incandescent readout segment through a transistor
circuits.description: A segment output drives an NPN switch through a base resistor; the collector pulls one filament segment of the readout down from the tube supply VT. One such stage serves each of the seven outputs. RCA Numitron DR2000 series readouts are named for it, needing VT = 3.5 V to 5 V and 24 mA per segment.
notes: Segment a stands for any of the seven outputs a to g, each with its own stage.
Transistor figures: βdc (min) ≥ 25, VCE(sat) ≤ 0.5 V, with VDD = 5 V (min), IB = 1 mA (min), IT = 24 mA (min).
CD4049UB figures for these readouts: VCC = 10 V (min), VO(0) ≤ 2 V, VT ≈ 3.5 V to 6 V.

circuits.title: Driving a low-power incandescent readout segment through an inverting buffer
circuits.description: A segment output drives one inverter of a CD4049UB powered from the tube supply VT. The inverter output sinks the segment current through a series resistor and one filament segment returned to VT, so a high segment output lights the segment. Pinlites INC series O and R readouts are named for it.
notes: Segment a stands for any of the seven outputs a to g, each with its own inverter.
Transistor figures: βdc (min) ≥ 30, VCE(sat) ≤ 0.5 V, with VCC ≥ 3.5 V (min), IB ≥ 0.25 mA (min), IT ≤ 7.5 mA.
CD4049UB figures: at VCC = 10 V (min), VO(0) ≤ 0.6 V; at VCC = 6 V (min), VO(0) ≤ 1 V, IT = 5 mA (min), VT ≈ 1.5 V to 3.5 V.

circuits.title: Driving a neon (nixie) readout segment through a high-voltage transistor
circuits.description: A segment output drives an NPN switch through a base resistor; the collector pulls one cathode of a neon readout down from a tube supply of about 170 V dc. One stage serves each output. The transistor must block more than VT and leak no more than 0.05 mA when off.
notes: Segment a stands for any of the seven outputs a to g, each with its own stage.
Tubes named: Alco Electronics MG19; Burroughs B5971, B7971, B8971.

circuits.title: Driving a low-voltage vacuum fluorescent readout directly
circuits.description: The seven segment outputs connect straight to the anode segments of a vacuum fluorescent readout. The counter runs on 13.5 V between VDD and VSS, and VSS sits about 4.5 V above ground on a zener, so a lit segment sees about 18 V and an unlit one about 4.5 V against the grounded filament. The filament is heated from 1.6 V ac or dc.
notes: 13.5 V logic voltage between VDD and VSS.
VON = 18 V gives medium brightness against a low ambient light background; segments show no noticeable glow at VOFF ≈ 4.5 V.

Tubes named: Tung-Sol DIGIVAC S/G type DT1704A or DT1705C; NEC type DG12E or LD915. They need 100 µA to 300 µA per segment at tube voltages of 12 V to 25 V, set by the brightness wanted, and 45 mA of filament current at 1.6 V ac or dc.

circuits.title: Dynamic power dissipation test circuit, CD4033B
circuits.description: A pulse generator clocks a CD4033B whose nine outputs each carry a load capacitance CL to ground. RBI is held at VDD and CLOCK INHIBIT, RESET and LAMP TEST at ground, so the counter runs and every output switches. Supply current is read on a meter IM in the VDD lead, bypassed by 500 µF; 0.1 µF decouples VDD at the chip.

operation.text: Each device is a five-stage Johnson decade counter followed by a decoder that turns the Johnson code into seven segment drives for one digit of a numeric display. Both have CLOCK, RESET and CLOCK INHIBIT inputs and CARRY OUT plus the seven segment outputs a to g. Every input has a CMOS protection network of diodes to VDD and VSS.

RESET high sets the counter to zero. With CLOCK INHIBIT low the count steps once on each rising CLOCK edge; with CLOCK INHIBIT high clock edges are ignored. Holding CLOCK high turns CLOCK INHIBIT into a falling-edge clock input. Gating inside the Johnson counter stops it locking into an illegal state, so the sequence always comes right. The CLOCK input has a Schmitt trigger and the clock rise and fall times are unlimited.
CARRY OUT runs one full cycle per ten clock cycles and clocks the next decade directly, so digits chain without extra logic.
A selected segment output goes high. On CD4033B this happens directly; on CD4026B only while DISPLAY ENABLE IN is high.

DISPLAY ENABLE IN low pulls all seven segment outputs low whatever the count, so the display draws power only while it is enabled, and digits can be multiplexed. CARRY OUT and UNGATED C SEGMENT OUT bypass this gating and run all the time, which divide-by-60 and divide-by-12 counters need.

Non-significant zeros of a multi-digit number can be blanked, so 0050.0700 on eight digits reads 50.07. On the integer side, tie RBI of the most significant digit low and feed each digit's RBO to the RBI of the next digit toward the decimal point. On the fraction side, tie RBI of the least significant digit low and feed each RBO to the RBI of the next digit toward the decimal point. To show the zero just before the point in a purely fractional number (0.7346), or the zero in a number like 763.0, tie that digit's RBI high instead. Blanking unneeded zeros saves display power.
LAMP TEST high overrides the decoder and drives all seven segment outputs high, for checking the display for faults.

The B-series outputs give about ten times the drive of the earlier A-series CD4026A and CD4033A. The interface buffers those parts needed are not required with the B types: they drive most display devices directly, especially above 10 V.
Counting is fully static, from dc to 6 MHz typical at VDD = 10 V.

High-voltage type rated to 20 V, with parameters given at 5 V, 10 V and 15 V. Quiescent current is tested on every part at 20 V. Outputs are symmetrical and standardized. The parts meet JEDEC Tentative Standard No. 13B for B-series CMOS devices.
Decade counting and frequency division with 7-segment decimal displays; clocks, watches and timers (divide by 60, 60 and 12 counter and display); counter and display driver for meters.

Quiescent current is measured with the inputs set in a fixed sequence of 1 and 0 states through switches; pin 14 is disconnected for CD4026B. Input current is measured one input at a time to both VDD and VSS, with every unused input tied to VDD or VSS.
Three 16-pin packages: E is the plastic DIP, NSR the SOP on tape and reel, PW and PWR the TSSOP (PWR on tape and reel).
